$comment: What llxterm's terminal core is held to. `cargo run --release --bin check` reads results/*.json and fails on any rule a run breaks. Change a number only together with its reason, in the change that moves it.

rules.about: Every engine takes in every workload without a panic, timed and in a process of its own.
On these workloads every engine ends on llxterm's screen and cursor, so the engines are compared doing the same work.
On every workload llxterm's core takes output at least as fast as vt100, the floor.
On every workload llxterm's core takes output at least as fast as alacritty_terminal, the core most terminals of its language are built on.

On every workload llxterm's core takes output at least this share of the fastest reference core's speed. Below 1: on cursor, tui and recorded sessions the fastest reference leads by up to a third (0.65x to 0.91x in the runs of 2026-11-23), and what is left of the gap is inside the terminal core library, which llxterm keeps (decided 2026-11-23); runs on this machine differ by a tenth, so the share held is below the lowest run seen.
A terminal of 120 by 40 with 10,000 rows of history holds at most this in llxterm's core, over the floor of its process, on every workload.
